title: 2012 AMC 8 Problem 11
statement: The mean, median, and unique mode of the positive integers \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) and \(x\) are all equal. What is the value of \(x?\)

solutions.text:
Every listed value except \(6\) appears once while \(6\) appears twice. If \(x\) equals any of the other listed values, then we have two modes, which means we do not have a unique mode. Otherwise, the only value that shows up more than once is \(6\) making that the unique mode. This also means \(6\) is the mean. Since there are \(7\) elements, the sum of the elements is \(6\cdot 7 = 42.\) The sum is also \[3+4+5+6+6+7+x\] \[= 31+x \]\[= 42,\] so \(x = 11.\)

Thus, the answer is D .
hints: The unique mode must be the repeated listed number.
If the mean is that number, the total sum is fixed.
